subject: Post-demo follow-up: sponsor KPIs, procurement playbook, and champion coaching
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@finservone.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & immediate next steps (FinservOne)

Thanks team — quick recap from this morning's demo with Maya (FinservOne) and initial asks for enabling her as the internal champion. Key points below, plus proposed next steps.

TL;DR:
- Champion: Maya Patel (Head of Data Ops) — enthusiastic and willing to lead an internal pilot.
- Economic buyer: Daniel Hughes (CFO) — cares about TCO, token unit costs, and predictable monthly commitments.
- Security/legal gates: CISO (Anika Rao) wants SOC2 scope, data residency confirmation, and list of encryption controls. Procurement will require an SLA appendix and our standard IP/data handling clauses.
- Decision criteria: (1) unit cost vs current self-hosting, (2) latency SLA for inference under 300ms median, (3) security/compliance evidence.

What Maya asked us to deliver this week:
1) One-pager for Daniel that boils down ROI and cost/levers (pref to share Mon internal finance check).
2) Procurement checklist + expected timeline (Procurement indicated a 4–6 week review once contract is circulated).
3) Redacted security questionnaire + SOC2 artifact links for Legal/CISO review.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (MVP + owners + dates), redacted_security_qs.pdf (SOC2 pointers), champion_one_pager.docx (draft).

Proposed next steps (internal):
- Laura: can you build a two-slide CFO summary with a 3-year TCO comparison (cloud + infra + Redwood hosted cost) by EOD Friday?
- Aditya: prep the procurement checklist and suggested contract language for SLA/uptime and data residency; include a short optional discount cadence for committed volume.
- Connor: I'll schedule a 30-min working session with Maya for Monday to walk through the one-pager and coach her on executive framing.

Notes for champion coaching (first pass):
- Frame the ask as: "Reduce predictable inference costs while moving latency-sensitive workloads off under-resourced infra."
- Quantify current spend: Maya estimated $28–32k/mo in infra + ops headcount; we should show 12–18 month payback scenarios for pilot scaling assumptions.
- Legal/Security language: emphasize that we support private VPC deployments and KMS integrations.

I'll drop the attachments to the shared Drive and send Maya a short checklist she can use with Procurement. Thoughts?

—Connor
Senior AE | Redwood Inference
(attachment stubs: mutual_action_plan.xlsx, redacted_security_qs.pdf, champion_one_pager.docx)

Thanks Connor — quick notes from procurement/finance angle:

- Procurement timeline: procurement@finservone.com indicated an "initial review" in 2 weeks if we can surface the SLA appendix and standard terms now. Full legal redline typically 4–6 weeks, but often faster if SOW/uptime items are pre-agreed.
- Discount recommendation: for a 6–12 month reserved capacity commit, offer a stepped discount: 10% in month 1–3, 15% after 3 months as usage stabilizes. That gives Daniel something conservative to approve upfront.
- CFO slide guidance (Connor's ask): include a single-cell sensitivity table showing result at +/- 20% inference volume and +/- 10% latency penalty (data ops risk).

I'll take Connor's ask on the CFO slides and will reuse the Cost Model template in the Drive. Expect a draft by Friday 18:00 PST.

Also flagged to Legal: can we prepare a short note on data residency options (multi-region hosting vs VPC)? They'll want the explicit language.

—Laura
Enterprise Sales Ops | Redwood Inference

Adding a short coaching note for Maya (copying below — we'll share as a one-pager she can forward):

Champion coaching bullets for internal outreach to CFO & Procurement:
- Subject lines to use: "Pilot to reduce inference ops cost — 90 day ROI outlook" OR "Controlled pilot: predictable latency & reduced infra spend"
- Opening line (to finance): "We're proposing a controlled pilot with Redwood Inference to reduce our inference spend while guaranteeing latency for customer-facing models — outline below with expected POC metrics."
- 3 quick slides for internal review: 1) Problem + current spend snapshot, 2) Pilot scope & KPIs (latency targets, throughput, success criteria), 3) Financial ask + payback table.
- ROI math (simple): show net cost delta = current infra ops run-rate + estimated ops FTE hours saved - Redwood monthly committed price. Use a low/central/high volume scenario.
- Redlines to watch for in contract: data deletion timelines, subprocessor list, incident notification SLA.

I'll draft the one-pager and attach a short script for Maya to paste into an internal email. Connor, if you want I can take the first draft of the champion_one_pager.docx and circulate to Maya for review tonight.

—Aditya
